title: Deployment lifecycle utility model and bundle recommendations
content:
Purpose and context:
This sheet is a working modeling artifact to compare full lifecycle costs (TCO) and ROI for Private deployments: On‑Prem (customer datacenter) versus VPC (customer-controlled cloud accounts). It combines hardware capex/maintenance, licensing + support bundles, operator FTEs, power/cooling, networking, and an uplift line for Redwood Optimize features (caching, batching, quantization) that reduce unit GPU-hours.

Goal:
- Produce break‑even analysis across 3 customer archetypes (startup, mid-market, enterprise) over a 5‑year horizon.
- Surface recommended license + support bundles (Standard, Plus, Enterprise) and suggested pricing bands and conditions.
- Highlight sensitivity to GPU utilization, refresh cadence, and support SLAs.

Assumptions (editable cells):
- time_horizon_years = 5
- discount_rate = 0.08
- hardware_refresh_cycle_years = 3
- avg_gpu_price_per_unit = $12,500
- avg_gpu_count_startup = 4, midmarket = 24, enterprise = 128
- avg_utilization_baseline = 0.35 (35% usable hours)
- optimize_feature_uplift = 0.18 (18% effective GPU-hour saving with Redwood Optimize recommendations)
- power_per_rack_kW = 35
- power_cost_per_kWh = $0.11 (on‑prem average); VPC power embedded in compute price
- ops_hourly_rate = $80 (fully loaded for infra engineer)
- ops_fte_per_50_gpus = 0.5
- support_premium_multiplier: Standard=1.0, Plus=1.35, Enterprise=1.9

Tabs included in the sheet (description):
- Overview: scenario selectors, high-level chart of cumulative costs, break-even year, key sensitivities.
- Inputs: editable assumption block (the list above plus region, tax, customs, facility lease).
- CapEx & Amortization: purchase schedule, per‑year depreciation, refresh replacements at year 3.
- OpEx: power, cooling, network, rack space, monitoring, backup, license renewals.
- People: onboarding, training, support HCC (headcount curve), on-call multipliers.
- Optimize Impact: modeled token/GPU-hour savings, cache hit-rate sensitivity table.
- Bundles: pricing recommendation calc, SLA mapping, deliverables per tier.
- Sensitivity: tornado charts for utilization, refresh cadence, power price, support uplift.
- Outputs: per-customer-type P&L style summary, NPV, payback period.

Sample CapEx table (tab: CapEx & Amortization) - CSV style excerpt:
entity,year,items,unit_cost,qty,total_cost,comment
startup,2025,GPU x A100-80GB,$12,500,4,$50,000,initial deployment
startup,2027,GPU refresh,$10,500,4,$42,000,refresh to next-gen compression-friendly chips
midmarket,2025,GPUs,$12,500,24,$300,000,1 rack + NVMe cache nodes
enterprise,2025,GPUs,$12,500,128,$1,600,000,multi-rack

OpEx example lines (tab: OpEx) - formulas in plain language:
- annual_power_cost_onprem = racks * power_per_rack_kW * 24 * 365 * power_cost_per_kWh * PUE
- vpc_compute_cost = quoted_cloud_cpu_gpu_hour_rate * predicted_gpu_hours (post-optimize uplift)
- network_egress_estimate = tb_per_month * egress_rate
- license_fee_yearly = base_license * support_premium_multiplier (per bundle)

Optimize uplift modeling note:
We model two levers: (1) steady-state optimize adoption (opt_adopt_pct) applied linearly to utilization; (2) feature maturity factor (ramping over 12 months). Practical formula used in sheet: effective_gpu_hours = raw_gpu_hours * (1 - optimize_feature_uplift * opt_adopt_pct * maturity_factor). We run low/med/high adoption scenarios: 5%, 40%, 75%.

Bundles and recommended structure (working draft):
- Standard (S): base platform license, email support, best-effort deployment guide. Target: startups. Suggested list price = per-GPU-month $55 (annual commit discount 20%).
- Plus (P): includes 8x5 SLA, 2 on-call incidents/month, onboarding assistance, quarterly performance review. Target: mid-market. Suggested list price = per-GPU-month $120 (annual commit discount 25%).
- Enterprise (E): 24x7 SLA, named SE, on-prem installation assistance, upgrade window guarantees, higher retention of logs. Target: regulated/large customers. Suggested list price = per-GPU-month $240 (negotiable, volume tiers and reserved capacity accounts).
Pricing notes: list prices are placeholders; actual final should tie to modeled savings from Optimize uplift and Customer's ops saving. For VPC we model a platform surcharge (Redwood managed control plane) as 8-12% of cloud compute spend. For On‑Prem we show equivalent amortized infra + ops + facilities.

Break-even heuristics and example output:
- For mid-market archetype with 24 GPUs at 35% baseline utilization, assuming optimize uplift 18% and 40% adoption ramp, on-prem becomes cost-effective versus VPC if cloud GPU-hour rate exceeds $0.85 (post-discounts) or if on-prem capital is financed at <7.5% over 3 years.
- Enterprise (128 GPUs) shows typical payback of 18-30 months for on-prem vs VPC at steady utilization >40%.

Sensitivity experiments to run (checklist):
- sensitivity matrix: x-axis = utilization [20%, 30%, 40%, 60%], y-axis = GPU price per hour [0.30, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25] -> heatmap of best deployment choice.
- refresh cadence impact: 2-year vs 3-year vs 4-year cycles on NPV and replacement capex smoothing.
- ops staffing model variance: ops_fte_per_50_gpus from 0.25 to 1.0.
- power cost shocks: +/- 30% for on-prem.
- optimize_feature_uplift sensitivity: 5%, 12%, 18%, 30%.

Unresolved questions / open items (actionable):
- Confirm typical GPU sku for buyer segment (A100-80GB vs H100 vs customer-owned older gen) -> owner: Marcus Hale, due 2025-02-10.
- Get 3 example VPC pricing quotes (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) for GPU reserved and spot rates -> owner: Jun Park, due 2025-02-14.
- Validate ops hourly fully-burdened rates in target region (Emea vs NA) -> owner: Elsa Romero, due 2025-02-12.
- Decide whether to include customs/tariff buffer for APAC on-prem purchases -> product decision required.

Quick wins (product asks):
- Add a small line in onboarding playbook for customers comparing bundle ROI at proof-of-concept stage (junior RM can use).
- Add Optimize checklist items into Plus bundle (automated quantization recommendations, batching profile templates).

Recommended next steps (short):
1) Lock down input interrogatories for pre-sales template (1‑pager with required fields to feed spreadsheet). Owner: Priya. Deadline: 1 week.
2) Run 3 VPC vendor quotes, populate region tab. Owner: Jun. 2 weeks.
3) Run sensitivity sweeps and produce break-even heatmap for midmarket and enterprise. Owner: Marcus + Data Science. 2 weeks.
4) Draft final bundle wording and attach SLA draft for legal review (Enterprise). Owner: Product lead. 3 weeks.

Notes to self / informal thoughts (scratchpad):
- Might add a small coefficient for depreciation tax benefit depending on customer jurisdiction (easy toggle).
- Consider variable for hidden overhead: internal change freeze windows add ~2x engineer hours/month during major upgrades.
- Customers often undervalue caching benefit because they assume stateless inference; model needs to surface the per-request token skew where caching produces >30% saving.

References and quick links (placeholders):
- Confluence: PD-architecture-deployments-2024 (link above)
- Jira: PD-1427 (linked) -> ticket describes enterprise install checklist
- GitHub: infra-deploy-simulations PR#86 -> contains earlier cost sim scripts

If you iterate on numbers put date + initials in a new row each time (ex: 2025-02-18 PD v0.2). Keep this file as the single source of truth for the modelling assumptions and recommended bundle starting points.

End of sheet draft.
